title: Write a Simple Message to a Text File
description: Write a C program that creates a file named 'message.txt' and writes the message 'Hello, C File Handling!' to it. Print a success message if the write was successful.
constraints: The output file must be named 'message.txt'. Content is fixed. Handle file open errors gracefully.
sampleOutput: Successfully wrote 'Hello, C File Handling!' to message.txt.
explanation: The output is shown if the message is written to the file as required.

title: Read and Display Entire Content of a Text File
description: Given a file named 'data.txt' (already present), write a C program that prints its entire contents, line by line.
constraints: The 'data.txt' file exists. Each line is up to 100 chars; at most 10 lines.
sampleOutput:
Content from data.txt:
This is line one.
This is line two.
explanation: The output matches the lines in 'data.txt'. Changing the file contents changes the output.

title: Append User Input to an Existing Log File
description: Write a C program that asks the user for two messages and appends each to 'activity_log.txt', printing a confirmation after each append.
constraints: Each message is a single line, max 80 chars. Demonstrate appending two messages.
sampleInput:
User logged in
Item added to cart
sampleOutput:
Message 'User logged in' appended to activity_log.txt.
Message 'Item added to cart' appended to activity_log.txt.
explanation: The output confirms the messages entered by the user are appended. Different messages change the output.

title: Count Lines in a Text File
description: Write a C program that prompts the user for a filename and prints the number of lines in that file.
constraints: Filename up to 50 chars. File may have up to 100 lines, each up to 200 chars.
explanation: The output shows the count of lines found in the file named by the user.

title: Copy Content from One Text File to Another
description: Write a C program that prompts for a source and destination filename, then copies all content from the source file to the destination file.
constraints: Filenames up to 50 chars. Source file is at most 1KB. Handle source file not found.
sampleOutput: Content successfully copied from original.txt to new_copy.txt.
explanation: The output confirms that the content was copied from the source file to the destination file.

title: Student Record Management using Text File (CSV Format)
description: Define a struct Student with roll_no, name, and gpa. Write a C program to accept up to 3 students' data, write to 'students.csv' in CSV format, then read and print all records.
constraints: Max 3 students. Roll No: 1-999. Name: max 30 chars. GPA: 0.0-4.0.
sampleOutput:
Student records successfully written to students.csv.

--- Student Records from File ---
Roll No: 101, Name: Alice, GPA: 3.75
Roll No: 102, Name: Bob, GPA: 3.50
Roll No: 103, Name: Charlie, GPA: 3.90
explanation: The output confirms records were written and read, matching the user input for each student.

title: Simple Data Logging with Binary Files
description: Write a C program that takes 5 integers as input, writes them to a binary file 'numbers.bin', then reads them back and prints them.
constraints: Input integers between -1000 and 1000. Use fwrite and fread correctly.
sampleOutput:
Successfully wrote 5 integers to numbers.bin.
Numbers read from numbers.bin: 10 20 30 40 50
explanation: The output shows the integers entered by the user and confirms they were stored and read from the file.

title: Search and Update a Record in a Text File
description: Given a 'products.txt' file where each line is 'ID,Name,Price', write a C program to update the price for a given product ID as entered by the user.
constraints: products.txt exists with 2-3 records. IDs unique. Name max 30 chars. Price 0.01-5000.00.
explanation: The output confirms the price for the product ID entered by the user is updated.

title: Random File Access using fseek() and ftell()
description: Write a C program that creates a file containing 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', then uses fseek to go to the 10th character and prints it and the file pointer position.
constraints: The string to write is fixed. File names are fixed. Content is ASCII.
sampleOutput:
Character at 10th position (index 9): J
Current file pointer position: 10
explanation: The output shows the character at the given position and the file pointer value.

title: Simple Command-Line To-Do List Manager
description: Write a C program providing a menu-driven interface to add tasks, view tasks, clear all tasks, or exit. Tasks are stored line by line in 'tasks.txt'.
constraints: Tasks up to 100 chars. tasks.txt max 10 tasks. Input is valid per menu choice.
sampleOutput:
--- To-Do List Menu ---
1. Add Task
2. View Tasks
3. Clear All Tasks
4. Exit
Enter your choice: 1
Enter new task: Buy groceries
Task 'Buy groceries' added.
Enter your choice: 1
Enter new task: Clean room
Task 'Clean room' added.
Enter your choice: 2
Tasks:
Buy groceries
Clean room
Enter your choice: 3
All tasks cleared.
Enter your choice: 2
No tasks found.
Enter your choice: 4
Exiting To-Do List Manager.
explanation: The output reflects actions taken by the user, based on the entered menu choices and tasks.
